Problem Statement:

Discussion: https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi/discussions/9744

turns.reply: The root cause is in `Dependant._unwrapped_call`: it calls `inspect.unwrap`, which does not look through `functools.partial`. So async and generator detection fail for partials of coroutine functions, generators, and callable classes. I'll make it unwrap partials first.

output.diff:
--- a//workspace/fastapi/dependencies/models.py
+++ b//workspace/fastapi/dependencies/models.py
@@ -79,7 +79,16 @@
     def _unwrapped_call(self) -> Any:
         if self.call is None:
             return self.call  # pragma: no cover
-        return inspect.unwrap(self.call)
+        unwrapped = self.call
+        while True:
+            if isinstance(unwrapped, functools.partial):
+                unwrapped = unwrapped.func
+                continue
+            new_unwrapped = inspect.unwrap(unwrapped)
+            if new_unwrapped is unwrapped:
+                break
+            unwrapped = new_unwrapped
+        return unwrapped
 
     @cached_property
     def is_gen_callable(self) -> bool:

turns.reply: Detection now works for every partial case in my check, and the existing class-dependency tests pass. Submitting.

`Dependant` now looks through `functools.partial` wrappers when deciding whether a dependable is async, a generator, or an async generator, so partials of async functions, generators, and callable classes are handled the same way as plain functions. The change is in `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`. A quick check of the partial cases gave the expected results, and the existing `test_dependency_class.py` tests pass. I did not run the full test suite or add tests for the partial cases.
